SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 3-day history of worsening headache, predominantly around right eye but “all over” head; constant with episodic intensification; current severity 8/10; dull baseline becoming sharp at times.
- Associated symptoms: photophobia (“bright light hurts”), intermittent “shooting lights”; feels nauseated but no vomiting; difficulty focusing; no visual loss, no speech disturbance, no limb weakness/numbness, no neck stiffness, no fever, no rash, no recent head injury.
- Aggravating factors: bright light; computer work.  
- Relieving factors tried: Ibuprofen self-administered 3 times/day x 2 days – minimal relief.
- Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses; no prior diagnosed migraines.
- Family history: Mother and sister with recurrent migraines.
- Medications: 
  • Ibuprofen (self-medicated) – dose/route/frequency not fully documented (patient taking 3 tablets/day).  
  • No regular prescription medications.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives with three housemates; works in IT (prolonged screen use); social smoker; drinks alcohol socially; mild recent work stress.

Objective:
- No vitals or physical examination findings documented.
- No investigations performed or available at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute headache
   - Assessment: Likely migraine-type headache.
   - Differential diagnosis: Tension-type headache, cluster headache, medication-overuse headache; secondary causes less likely given history (intracranial pathology, infection) but to monitor.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Educated patient on optimal NSAID dosing: Ibuprofen up to 400 mg PO three times daily with food (if tolerated) OR prescribe Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
     • May add Paracetamol and/or Codeine for breakthrough pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
     • Advised maintaining hydration, reducing screen brightness, resting in dark room as needed.  
   - Follow-up: Keep headache diary to identify triggers; review in 1–2 weeks.  
   - Safety-netting: Return sooner or call if headache worsens, vision changes, focal neurologic deficits, vomiting, fever, or other concerning symptoms.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: No vital signs, neurological or fundoscopic examination documented; medication doses not specified for new prescriptions; formal migraine diagnostic criteria not fully documented.  
● Internal conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal irrelevant noise; no inaudible sections.
